description: Genuine Bazel 9.3.1 (bazel-9.3.1-linux-x86_64, --batch --ignore_all_rc_files, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, --registry=tests/fixtures/builtin_modules/registry --lockfile_mode=off) `test //pkg:all --remote_cache=http://127.0.0.1:PORT` against an empty HTTP cache, then again with a fresh output root against the populated cache. Test spawns go through RemoteSpawnCache: the AC keys of the TestRunner spawns (test-setup.sh) and the XML generating spawns (generate-xml.sh) per target, from --execution_log_json_file. //pkg:bad fails (its test spawn is not uploaded), //pkg:nrc is tagged no-remote-cache (neither spawn uses the cache), //pkg:ext is tagged external (its test spawn carries no-cache; its XML spawn is cached).

files.pkg/tests.bzl:
def _t(ctx):
    out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.label.name + ".sh")
    ctx.actions.write(out, "#!/bin/bash\necho testing; cat pkg/in.txt; echo out > $TEST_UNDECLARED_OUTPUTS_DIR/u.txt; echo err >&2; if [ -n \"$WRITE_XML\" ]; then echo '<testsuites/>' > $XML_OUTPUT_FILE; fi; [ -n \"$TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE\" ] && touch $TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE; exit $1\n", is_executable = True)
    return [DefaultInfo(executable = out, runfiles = ctx.runfiles(files = ctx.files.data)), RunEnvironmentInfo(environment = ctx.attr.env)]
t_test = rule(_t, test = True, attrs = {"data": attr.label_list(allow_files = True), "env": attr.string_dict()})
